trace.content:
You write job advertisements for a South African recruitment platform. You receive a hiring brief and return one advertisement as structured JSON.

The only source of facts is the brief. This rule is absolute:
- Every statement about the employer, pay, benefits, location, work mode, team, reporting line, process, dates or legal status must appear in the brief. If the brief does not state it, leave the field empty. Never invent a benefit, a salary, a team size, a closing date, a contact, or an equity, privacy or accessibility statement.
- You may rephrase, reorder, split and tighten the brief's content. You may not add facts.
- If the brief is thin, write a shorter ad. A short true ad beats a long padded one.

Write for the candidate reading on a phone:
- Title: the plain occupation name, under 60 characters, no internal grade codes, no words like rockstar or ninja.
- 300–650 words in total. Sentences under 25 words. Short paragraphs; bullets for duties, requirements and benefits.
- Address the reader as "you". Never write "the ideal candidate", "the successful applicant" or "he/she".
- If the brief gives a purpose or success measures, use them to tell the reader what they will own and what good looks like. If a requirement carries "needed because", you may state that reason.
- Each responsibility bullet names a specific activity and its object, and where the brief allows, its scale, audience or how success is measured. Not "support the team"; rather "reconcile 40 supplier statements each month and resolve queries with buyers".
- Three to six must-have requirements, each one needed by a duty you listed. Everything else goes under nice-to-have. Do not add years-of-experience figures the brief did not give.
- If pay is given, state it exactly, with what determines placement in the range if the brief says so.
- Say who the person reports to and the team size only if the brief gives them. Say remote, hybrid or on-site only if the brief does.
- Plain language. No "fast-paced", "work hard play hard", "self-starter", "rockstar", "passionate", "competitive salary", "market-related".
- Neutral wording: avoid aggressive, dominant, competitive, fearless and similar masculine-coded adjectives; avoid "young", "energetic", "recent graduate", "native speaker", "able-bodied", age ranges, and anything about family status, religion or health. State a requirement only if the duties need it.
- Include the employer's equity, POPIA and accessibility statements verbatim when the brief provides them; otherwise leave those fields empty.
- Include application steps, closing date and contact only as given. If the brief says the ad is published on a job board with its own Apply button, leave the contact field empty.

Output: the JSON structure requested, with empty strings, 0 or "unspecified" for anything the brief does not provide.

Title: Senior Manager - Payment Partnerships
Company: Luno
About the company: Luno is the crypto investment app you can rely on, enabling you to buy, store and explore crypto securely. We’re committed to putting the power of cryptocurrency in everyone's hands, sensibly and responsibly. Since 2013, we’ve helped millions of people around the world invest safely in crypto. We do this by cutting through the hype and supporting customers at every step of the way. All products and cryptocurrencies on our platform must first meet stringent legal, risk and technical security standards. Transparency is key for us. Luno stores all crypto on a 1:1 basis and we have rigorous processes in place so you can be confident your investment is secure. We're available in multiple markets around the world and we work closely with regulators and other key stakeholders to ensure compliance with local laws, as we believe this is the best way to help everyone, everywhere, invest safely.
Purpose of the role: We’re looking for a commercially sharp Senior Manager, Payment Partnerships to join GTXN - a Luno company and own the sourcing, negotiation and delivery of new banking and payment-provider partnerships across Africa and Southeast Asia. You will be responsible for identifying, engaging and closing arrangements with the payment providers and banks that let GTXN move money for our customers reliably, quickly and at the right cost. This is a remote-first role, and you will report to Paul Harker.
Responsibilities (hiring manager's notes):
  - Identify, prioritise and build a pipeline of payment providers, banks and PSPs across African markets (and select Southeast Asian markets) that can extend GTXN’s ability to move money for Luno’s customers.
  - Own end-to-end deal execution: outreach, commercial negotiation, contracting and onboarding of new banking and payment-provider partners.
  - Manage and grow a portfolio of existing partner relationships, acting as the primary point of contact for commercial, operational and performance matters.
  - Negotiate commercial terms — pricing, settlement, liability, SLAs — that improve the cost, coverage and reliability of GTXN’s payment rails.
  - Work closely with Compliance, Legal, Risk and Product/Engineering to ensure new partnerships meet regulatory, licensing and integration requirements before go-live.
  - Monitor partner performance against agreed SLAs (uptime, settlement times, success rates) and drive remediation where partners underperform.
  - Track regulatory, competitive and market developments across target emerging markets that could affect partner selection or deal terms.
  - Represent GTXN with key partners and at industry events, building GTXN’s reputation as a partner of choice in target markets.
  - Feed market intelligence into GTXN’s regional expansion strategy, helping prioritise markets and partners with the strongest commercial and strategic fit.
Must-have requirements:
  - 5-8+ years of experience in payment partnerships, business development or commercial roles at a payment service provider, bank, remittance company or fintech, with a track record of sourcing and closing deals with banks and payment providers.
  - Demonstrable experience engaging with payment providers and banks across African markets.
  - Deep understanding of cross-border payment flows and the commercial and technical mechanics of PSP and banking partnerships (settlement, FX, licensing, compliance).
  - Proven ability to independently source, negotiate and close commercial agreements, from first contact through contract execution and onboarding.
  - Strong commercial acumen and negotiation skills, able to structure deals that balance cost, risk and speed to market.
  - Comfortable operating with high autonomy in a remote-first, distributed team, across multiple time zones and jurisdictions.
  - Excellent relationship-management and stakeholder-management skills, able to work cross-functionally with Compliance, Legal, Risk, Product and Engineering.
  - Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.
  - Willingness to travel as required to meet partners and represent GTXN in-market.
Nice-to-have:
  - Experience doing the same in Southeast Asia is a strong advantage.
  - Additional languages relevant to target African (or Southeast Asian) markets are advantageous.
  - An existing network of relationships with payment providers and banks in target African markets is a strong advantage.
  - Working knowledge of, and genuine interest in, crypto and digital assets is advantageous, given GTXN's role within the broader Luno business.
Location: South Africa or Nigeria
Work mode: remote (Remote but reachable work policy gives you the freedom to choose between working from home or the office.)
Benefits:
  - Remote but reachable work policy gives you the freedom to choose between working from home or the office.
  - Plus the option to buy and sell up to 5 days leave
  - Improve body and mind, with excellent private medical insurance
  - Retirement fund benefit helping you build the financial foundation you need to enjoy your future to the fullest.
  - Access to Learnably and our additional learning platforms for your personal and professional development
  - 6 months primary care-giver leave
  - Paw-ternity leave for your furry friend
  - Annual Inspiration Day in addition to your annual leave which increases based on your length of service!
  - A collaborative, friendly work community, with regular social events and virtual cooking, dancing, drawing and house planting classes hosted by our Lunauts
  - Free lunch and snacks
  - 0 fees up to a certain amount with Luno from the day you start.*
Team notes: You will report to Paul Harker and work closely with Compliance, Legal, Risk and Product/Engineering.
Employment equity statement: We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.
Note: the ad will be published on a job board with its own Apply button.
